[DoVer](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.06749) optimizes per-trial message or plan edits, not model weights or a distilled skill. It segments failed trajectories at replans and contrasts each replay with its original failure; no paired success–failure alignment is specified (§4.1, lines 00134–00151).

Replay restores prior context and state, including browsing history; milestone evaluation aligns traces with human-derived, tool-agnostic milestones. Neither specifies functional program-state alignment across trajectories (§4.1, line 00135; Appendix B, line 01163).

Interventions receive three independent runs. Success, LLM-judged fulfillment and milestone progress classify hypotheses, rather than select a reusable skill (§4.2, lines 00153–00172). This overlaps trajectory distillation in extracting actionable information, teacher guidance through generated instructions and curated examples, fixed-model adaptation through message edits, and skill verification through execution-based testing—but does not establish skill distillation or cross-task transfer (§5.3, lines 00284–00285).

Authors report transfer across two frameworks and 29–67% inconclusive outcomes; checkpoint engineering, textual intervention limits and LLM judges constrain generality (§5.5, lines 00301–00303; §7, lines 00308–00310). We did not replicate these claims. The paper does not test our fixed-evidence, fixed-budget functional-state-versus-chronological comparison.
